quizzes.stem: Scenario: Dmitri's company wants developers limited to two approved models. The platform team sets `model` to the first of them in the managed file and tells the developers to use only those two. What happens when a developer picks another model?

options.a: It is allowed, since only a list in the policy restricts such a choice
options.b: The choice is refused, because the managed file outranks the developer's own picks
options.c: The pick is refused for the session and restored after the next restart
options.d: The pick stands only if the project file also names that model

explanation.a: A managed `model` is a default, and the lock is the list.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A managed `model` is a **default**: a developer can still pick another model".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Neither choice is temporary", and a default refuses nothing that a restart could lift.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "a default is overridden at once", whatever the project file names.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Amara adds `allowManagedHooksOnly: true` to the shared project file that Amara's team commits, expecting every developer to be limited to the hooks of the organisation. What is the effect?

options.a: Only the organisation's hooks run, since the team's file outranks the user file
options.b: Every hook is switched off in the project until the managed file confirms it
options.c: Nothing changes for anyone, since only the top tier reads that key
options.d: Only the hooks of the project run, since the team's choice is the closest

explanation.c: A lower file that sets a managed-only key has no effect.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "a lock written in the shared project file looks like policy and does nothing", whatever the order of the files below the managed level.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A lower file that sets one of these has **no effect**", so no hook is switched off and nothing waits for confirmation.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Some keys are read only from managed settings, because their purpose is to be out of a developer's reach".

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Yusuf's organisation limit is 20000 a month and covers three groups. Yusuf proposes limits of 7000, 8000 and 6000 for them. Under this module's rule for spend limits, how should that proposal be judged?

options.a: It is sound, because the organisation limit stops any overspend by the groups
options.b: It breaks the arithmetic, since the parts could together exceed the whole
options.c: It is sound, because unused budget of one group is lent to the others
options.d: It is inconsistent, since each group must have the same limit as the others

explanation.b: Seven thousand, eight thousand and six thousand add up to 21000, which is more than 20000.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "so the organisation limit would decide before the group limits did and nobody would know which one they were under".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Both are checked as a boundary: a total of exactly 20000 passes and 20001 does not", so a total of 21000 fails whatever happens to unused budget.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page's own example has "three groups with 6000, 8000 and 6000 against an organisation limit of 20000", so equal limits are not required.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: A platform team wants to show leadership that Claude Code is working. It sets a target of more accepted lines per developer each month and starts the rollout on Monday. By the measures this module teaches, what is the main weakness of the plan?

options.a: Accepted lines are not shown on the dashboard and cannot be tracked
options.b: Accepted lines need the GitHub app, which the plan has not set up
options.c: It counts accepted lines where daily active users show an outcome
options.d: It is met by taking extra suggestions while merges stay as slow

explanation.d: A target on an activity rewards the activity itself, so it can be met while pull requests merge no sooner, and nothing measured shows a result.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "The dashboard counts lines accepted as a usage metric".
explanation.c: Ruled out because daily active users sit in the same list as lines accepted, "Usage metrics (lines accepted, suggestions accepted, daily active users, sessions)", which measure activity too and show no outcome.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Contribution metrics need the GitHub app", and lines accepted are a usage metric, not one of those contribution metrics.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: An organisation's managed settings name its approved MCP servers in `allowedMcpServers`. A developer's laptop still uses a server that appears only in their own user file. Which fact explains it?

options.a: The user file outranks the managed file for any server it names
options.b: Managed settings take no server keys, so the managed list was ignored
options.c: The two allowlists combined, since nothing locks them to one source
options.d: The user file was read last, so its entries replaced the managed ones

explanation.c: Without `allowManagedMcpServersOnly`, a list combines across files, so the developer's own entry widens the managed allowlist.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the administrator "can restrict MCP servers to a managed allowlist", so the managed list is read and applies alongside the developer's own.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "no user, project or local value overrides it" for the managed level.
explanation.d: Ruled out because a list "is combined across files and not replaced".

quizzes.stem: Scenario: A company's managed plugin allowlist names only its own marketplace, yet some developers still try unreviewed plugins by starting a session with an option that pulls one in from a local folder. Which managed key closes that gap?

explanation.b: A plugin loaded from a folder for one session comes in through a sideload flag, and that key rejects those flags.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "the allowlist does not stop a developer from loading a plugin from a folder for one run with a command-line flag".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "only managed hooks run" is all that key does, and the plugin's skills and agents still load.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "only the managed `allowedMcpServers` list applies", which governs servers and leaves the plugin's skills and agents loaded.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Following this module's rollout plan, a team records four weeks of the time to merge for pull requests before the rollout starts. Why four weeks, and what does the record allow later?

options.a: Because usage credits reset every four weeks and the data must match
options.b: Because the dashboard keeps only four weeks, so older data is lost
options.c: Because a month evens out weekly noise, so no outcome target is needed
options.d: Because it spans a release cycle, so any shift is measured against it

explanation.d: A baseline with a release cycle in it lets a later change be measured.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page says "enough to include a release cycle and a quiet week", not a limit of the dashboard.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the plan "states two outcome targets: the share of merged pull requests with assistance, and the time to merge".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "the baseline of four weeks and the way the limits add up are this course's design values", not a cycle of usage credits.
